title: Case split on the degree d < 3 vs 3 ≤ d in the Friendship Theorem
intent: Reduce the Friendship Theorem to two closed branches by first extracting the regular degree d from the no-politician assumption, then splitting on d < 3 vs 3 ≤ d, closing the small-degree side by a constructive lemma and the large-degree side by a contradiction.
also_known_as: branch on d < k vs k ≤ d

children.name: isRegularOf_not_existsPolitician
children.statement: theorem isRegularOf_not_existsPolitician (hG' : ¬ExistsPolitician G) : ∃ d : ℕ, G.IsRegularOfDegree d
children.closed_by: by_cases on G.Adj v x, G.Adj x w, G.Adj v y; each branch closed by degree_eq_of_not_adj (lines 154-165), the last via a commonNeighbors cardinality argument (lines 167-175)

children.name: false_of_three_le_degree
children.statement: theorem false_of_three_le_degree (hd : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) (h : 3 ≤ d) : False
children.closed_by: contrapose! on ZMod.trace_pow_card, then a trace computation (trace_adjMatrix vs adjMatrix_pow_mod_p_of_regular) closed by lia (line 273)

children.name: existsPolitician_of_degree_le_two
children.statement: theorem existsPolitician_of_degree_le_two (hd : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) (h : d ≤ 2) : ExistsPolitician G
children.closed_by: interval_cases d; iterate 2 apply existsPolitician_of_degree_le_one; exact existsPolitician_of_degree_eq_two

applicability.goal_shape: A theorem whose conclusion depends only on a natural-number degree d that the proof first extracts from an assumption (here ∃ d, G.IsRegularOfDegree d), then branches on a threshold of d (d < 3 vs 3 ≤ d via lt_or_ge d 3).
applicability.use_when: the integer parameter has a genuine threshold: one side closes by a constructive existence lemma and the other by deriving a contradiction, so the two branches are unrelated sub-arguments each worth a named lemma.
applicability.avoid_when: the threshold is not a real cut between a constructive and an impossible case (one branch may be vacuous); the branches share substantial proof; or the exhaustiveness of the split (here lt_or_ge d 3) is not already a library fact.

claims.claim: The parent friendship_theorem closes from the three named child lemmas in six lines of glue (lines 330-335): isRegularOf_not_existsPolitician supplies the degree, lt_or_ge d 3 splits, and each branch is closed by one exact applying a child lemma.

The two goals produced by rcases lt_or_ge d 3 are d < 3 and 3 ≤ d; the first closes with exact npG (hG.existsPolitician_of_degree_le_two dreg (Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp dle2)) (line 334) and the second with exact hG.false_of_three_le_degree dreg dge3 (line 335).

The theorem's docstring states the plan the proof realises: 'If the degree is at most 2, we observe by casework that it has a politician anyway. If the degree is at least 3, the graph cannot exist.' (lines 328-329), matching the module outline 'By casework, show that if d = 0, 1, 2, then G has a politician. If 3 ≤ d, let p be a prime factor of d - 1.' (lines 29-30).

The longest chain of project lemmas below friendship_theorem is six deep: friendship_theorem (L330) → existsPolitician_of_degree_le_two (L315, calls existsPolitician_of_degree_eq_two at L319) → existsPolitician_of_degree_eq_two (L306, calls neighborFinset_eq_of_degree_eq_two at L310) → neighborFinset_eq_of_degree_eq_two (L289, calls card_of_regular at L298) → card_of_regular (L185, calls adjMatrix_sq_of_regular at L188) → adjMatrix_sq_of_regular (L127, calls adjMatrix_sq_of_ne at L131) → adjMatrix_sq_of_ne (L82, a leaf).

metrics.how_counted: parent = lines 330-335; direct children = the three named lemmas the glue calls; child_lines = full proof span of each child as copied (isRegularOf_not_existsPolitician 149-175, false_of_three_le_degree 248-273, existsPolitician_of_degree_le_two 315-319)

consequences: Creates two goals plus an exhaustiveness obligation, discharged by the library lemma lt_or_ge d 3. The witness d must be obtained before the split (isRegularOf_not_existsPolitician), so the glue depends on that lemma's signature. The d < 3 branch is re-encoded to d ≤ 2 via Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp before invoking its lemma, a coercion the author supplies by hand; if the threshold were stated as a ≤ on both sides this step would vanish.
